headline: Council approved $375,000 for affordable housing at 622 Auburn Street and authorized mayor's testimony on CMP power line project.
summary: Residents urged the council to oppose CMP's proposed transmission line project. The council unanimously authorized the mayor to testify to the Public Utilities Commission on the project. It also approved $375,000 for affordable housing at 622 Auburn Street and ratified a settlement with a tenants union.
decisions: Approved liquor license applications on the consent calendar, unanimously.
Approved resolve requesting ordinance changes regulating data centers, unanimously.
Approved mayor's testimony to the Public Utilities Commission on CMP transmission upgrades, unanimously.
Approved an amendment removing the Peaks Island Council's direct access to the council agenda, unanimously.
Approved council rules change on Peaks Island Council recommendations, as amended.
Ratified the settlement agreement among the city, Jeffrey Rice, and the Trilani Tenants Union, unanimously, as an emergency.
Approved an amendment to the Boyd and Cumberland affordable housing tax increment financing district, unanimously.
Approved an amended credit enhancement agreement for the Boyd and Cumberland housing project, unanimously.
Approved $375,000 from the housing trust fund for affordable housing at 622 Auburn Street, 7-0 by roll call.
Approved a third modification to the Forest Avenue pedestrian crossing project, adding about $17,000 in city funds, unanimously.
Adopted training procedures for Civilian Police Review Board members, unanimously.
Approved accepting and appropriating a federal firefighter grant as an emergency, 7-0 by roll call.
Approved accepting and appropriating a Department of Health and Human Services drug-free communities grant as an emergency, 7-0 by roll call.
discussion: CMP transmission line project: Many residents said they learned about the project late. They asked the council to oppose it as proposed and to push for independent review of need and alternatives.

Peaks Island Council agenda access: Members debated whether direct access to the agenda could open the door to other groups. Speakers argued the group has a charter role and an ordinance role that other groups lack.
Data center rules: A resident asked the council to regulate data centers completely out of Portland, citing the human cost of generative AI.
Downtown drug use and homelessness: A resident said open drug use on Commercial Street made them feel unsafe and urged the city to pair police with social workers, as Denver does.
Tenant settlement: Members called the agreement a win for tenants and asked that some rent control rulings be used as precedent.
